articleTitle: Effect of In-Situ Native Oxide Clean on Point Defect Behavior in Si+ Amorphized Ion-Implanted Si
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Mitigation of parasitic contact resistances require processing techniques that yield highly doped junctions such as ultra-shallow ion implantation. The depth of these junctions is so shallow that the role of the native oxide warrants further study. Investigation of an in-situ native oxide clean prior to amorphizing the surface of Si with 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Si<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions at an energy of 5 keV has been studied. HRTEM confirmed that, when the native oxide is present under these conditions, the amorphization process is incomplete, leaving near-surface crystallites embedded in the amorphous layer. However, when the oxide is removed in-situ, the samples had a continuous amorphous layer with no crystallites for the exact same implant conditions. This is the opposite of what is expected from damage simulations. Experiments with a plasma treatment and regrowth of the oxide prior to implantation show the complete amorphization process still occurs. It is proposed that hydrogen incorporation during plasma treatment may be reducing I-V recombination during the dynamic annealing stage of the implant leading to more effective amorphization. SRIM and FLOOXS simulations will be shown that support this model.

articleTitle: Impact of Lot Arrival Density Fluctuations on Cycle Time Control : IE: Industrial Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: For optimized cycle time control, a precise under-standing of lot arrival times is critical. Queueing theory has been used as a lightweight model for estimating WIP (work-in-progress) arrivals in fabs, typically under the highly simplified assumption that lot arrivals follow the Poisson process. This paper investigates the impact of lot arrival density fluctuations on manufacturing cycle time. Motivated by the observation that actual lot arrival times often exhibit clustering behavior, we propose using the Hawkes process to describe the stochasticity of lot arrivals. Our empirical evaluation on NY CREATES fab data shows that: 1) the Hawkes process offers a better fit than the Poisson process, and 2) this clustering behavior leads to increases in both WIP and cycle time, as demonstrated through WIP simulation.

articleTitle: Accelerated defectivity monitoring in high-volume manufacturing via unsupervised AI techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We present an innovative framework that leverages novel unsupervised AI techniques to automate defectivity setup in IC chip manufacturing. This new approach minimizes the need for expert intervention and eliminates redundant inspector-SEM review loops. With shorter time-to-results, the Fab productivity during the ramp-up phase can be greatly improved. This modern framework ultimately helps in bringing the industry closer to the vision of fully automated factory operation, allowing end users to focus more effectively on yield analysis.

articleTitle: The utilization of mathematical trends to characterize equipment manipulation at process temperature for leveling a CVD film
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Hot leveling is a mechanical process to improve the uniformity of a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) film. The current process is subjective and time consuming. This paper discusses the development of a mathematical model that represents the inside of the chamber which in turn gives the ability to create an innovative calculator for the hot leveling process. The calculator system will be integrated into a streamlined user interface for quick use by fab equipment technicians. The benefits of using this web-based calculator system will result in the improved quality of CVD films, a decrease in manpower hours working on the hot leveling process, and an increase in tool availability when recovering from maintenance.

articleTitle: OCD -Machine learning based metrology for copper pad surface for hybrid bonding integration
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the context of 3D hybrid bonding architectures, ensuring the flatness of metallic pads before bonding is critical. The control of this flatness is important and the dimension to be measured is very small (~nm) compared to the dimensions of the pattern (~µm). Traditional control methods, such as Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), offer high precision but lack the throughput required for high-volume manufacturing. Spectroscopic reflectometry (SR) presents an attractive metrological method due to its speed and larger measurement coverage. This study investigates the sensitivity of SR to dishing of copper pad across wafers with different thicknesses. We evaluate the ability of using a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model trained on raw spectra to predict copper dishing, using AFM as the reference measurement. Additionally, we assess whether the model can be extended to new batches of wafers and capture process variations. This study examines the capabilities of the deep learning based-model robustness predict the dishing of copper pads across varying experimental conditions.

articleTitle: Epi Defect Quantification via Massive Metrology SEM Measurement-Based Inspection
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this study, a comprehensive analysis of epitaxial (epi) defect detection and characterization in semiconductor wafers used in nanosheet logic devices is presented. The wafers, featuring layers of n-type epi and p-type epi, exhibited various defects due to the novel deposition process. These defects included missing epi, overgrown epi, and merged epi. Traditional defect review scanning electron microscope (SEM) tools, which compare defective sites to "good" sites, proved inadequate due to the high defect density across the wafer. Consequently, we employed a SEM tool capable of massive metrology, enabling the measurement of gray levels, areas, and distances between epi sites. This approach provided detailed defect maps, quantifying the extent and distribution of missing, overgrown, and merged epi defects. Our findings demonstrate that the massive metrology SEM tool offers superior accuracy in process characterization for wafers with rampant unstable epi growth compared to conventional SEM defect review methods. This research is significant as it enhances our understanding of epi defect trends and supports the development of more reliable semiconductor manufacturing processes, potentially leading to higher yield and performance in advanced logic devices.

articleTitle: A hybrid Cu-Al BEOL process for cost effective and efficient tool utilization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the implementation of a successful Cu-Al hybrid backend of line (BEOL) interconnect scheme for 0.13um process. Cu-Al hybrid process was used effectively to combine the advantages of both metals to lower cost of manufacturability and reduction in mask layers. A hybrid process also utilizes existing Aluminum tools efficiently for interconnects in wider via and top metal layer. Mask data preparation, suitable alignment structures and other details are also discussed. A reliable barrier process is employed to ensure a stable Cu-Al interface, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of the interconnects. SRAM Yield, Stress, electromigration lifetimes and MIM time dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) lifetimes were also tested. This study demonstrates a promising approach to achieving cost effective BEOL process for consumer applications.

articleTitle: Influence of Salicide Block Oxide and Key Process Parameters on P+ Polysilicon Resistor Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Polysilicon resistors are extensively used in integrated circuits due to their superior linearity, lower temperature coefficient, enhanced process compatibility, higher sheet resistance, and reduced chip area. This paper presents an indepth analysis of the effects of various processes on P+ poly resistors, focusing on poly film thickness, poly grain size, source-drain doping, spike annealing temperature, refractive index (RI) of Salicide block (SAB) film, stress of the contact etch stop nitride layer, clean reworks, and process resequencing. For the first time, we report on the impact of the PECVD SAB oxide film RI on P+ poly sheet resistance. The PECVD deposition process parameters, such as bias power and the spacing between the showerhead and wafer, can be adjusted to change the RI of the film and thus the sheet resistance. Our findings reveal that the SAB film RI is the most sensitive parameter for P+ poly resistors and can be independently tuned with minimal impact on other devices. SIMS analysis confirmed that the RI of the film influences the boron diffusion from silicon to SAB oxide. This study provides a novel and efficient method for process tuning and control of P+ poly resistors, offering valuable insights into optimizing resistance values through precise adjustment of deposition process parameters.

articleTitle: Full Wafer Inspection for Voltage Contrast Systematic Defects Using High-Throughput Point Scan
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A next generation system and methodology for high-throughput e-beam hot spot inspection is described. Rather than capturing images of each hot spot, just a single pixel centered on the signal node of each hot spot is collected and used to assess if the hot spot is defective or not. This innovation results in a very substantial savings in time per hot spot, and therefore a tremendous increase in throughput over previous generation hot spot inspection systems. Additional throughput improvement is gained by moving the stage continuously under the wafer, commonly referred to as continuous scan, as these individual pixels (aka points) are collected. Throughputs of 1 billion hot spots per hour are routinely achieved. The process for selecting hot spots for optimal scan speed and learning is explained. Back-end-of-line (BEOL) defects are binned based on unique path, allowing the source of primary defectivity to be statistically determined. Application of this system to a metal 2 missing-metal-fill defect issue affecting a recent Intel technology is described. By leveraging this system and split experiments involving progressively more stressed wafers, a 6 orders-of-magnitude drop in defectivity was accomplished relatively quickly preparing this technology for high-volume-manufacturing.

articleTitle: eFUSE and IDDQ Process Window Enhancement Through CoSi RTA Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: eFUSE technology has become integral in consumer and automotive applications, where electromigration of silicide is used to transition from a low to a high resistance state. The integration of a cobalt silicide (CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) process module is critical for ensuring process robustness and wafer yield. While a thicker cobalt silicide layer is preferred for maintaining low and stable pre-programming resistance, it poses a risk of increased junction leakage, subsequently degrading IDDQ leakage performance. Among the critical process variables, cobalt thickness, Rapid thermal annealing-1 (RTA1), and HF pre-clean processes are frequently optimized by process engineers to improve the process robustness and process margin. This paper discusses the optimization of the CoSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> RTA2 temperature to improve eFUSE performance without compromising the IDDQ leakage or sheet resistance requirements. The improved process window and robustness eliminate both eFUSE and IDDQ-related yield loss, ensuring reliability in various applications.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Epi Base Thickness of SiGe HBTs in BiCMOS Process: A Quest for Device Leakage Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We report some interesting observations on the junction leakage characteristics of SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) in BiCMOS technology node when the thickness of cap at the emitter-base (E-B) junction and spacer at the collector-base (C-B) junction were varied from their original thicknesses of Process of Record (POR). While preserving the total intrinsic base width, our work shows a possible improvement in the transistor junction leakage and breakdown voltage, despite some trade-offs which could be reoptimised by making slight modifications to the process. Our study provides a holistic understanding of the complex interdependence between thickness modulations in the epitaxial base and device characteristics in advanced SiGe HBTs.

articleTitle: Effect of Deposition Conditions on Polysilicon PNP Emitter Grain and Electrical Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the effect of the polysilicon emitter deposition conditions on the electrical performance and emitter film quality of a PNP transistor. An increase in the deposition temperature is seen to improve the gain of the transistor. The sheet resistance, breakdown voltage and Gummel plots were analysed to establish the mechanism for higher gain. TEM (Transmission Electron Microscopy) and XRD (X-ray Diffraction) techniques were used to characterize the emitter film, and SIMS (Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry) analysis was done to check the dopant profile at the emitter-base junction. The improvement in gain provides a better margin from the lower specification limit provided by the customer, along with an improvement in the range of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">be</inf> (base-to-emitter voltage) over which the transistor can be operated.

articleTitle: Optimization of D0 Performance in LPCVD Nitride through Implementation of Ammonia Purge
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work focused on the improvement on defectivity and the prolongation of process cycle by the implementation of ammonia purging process that optimized the D0 performance in Low Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) Nitride process. This is important to achieve consistent semiconductor wafer productibility with stable D0 performance process. Nitride was processed in the vertical furnace by LPCVD method at the temperature of 700°C to 760°C. Nitride was processed continuously and film was deposited until a fixed target cumulative thickness limit in the furnace, with no conditioning along the whole process cycle until maximum target cumulative thickness achieved or before furnace perform for preventive maintenance. However, the accumulation of nitride deposition induced defective particles in the furnace when it approached the end of process cycle due to film stress accumulation. The stress increased gradually resulted in particles flaking caused process cycle need to be terminated which unable to continue deposition to maximum target cumulative thickness. The proposed method to improve D0 performance for process prolongation was carried out ammonia purge conditioning in between process cycle at the 57%, 86% and 100% interval of nitride cumulative thickness. The ammonia gas was introduced into the furnace tube at temperature higher than 760°C process temperature, which was relatively higher than the LPCVD nitride process temperature. Ammonia then reacted with defects or impurities to form a stable product and exhaust by purging, resulted in a more defect-free environment in the process tube. Ammonia purge conditioning was found to have a significant effect on particles expelled and furnace tube cleanliness controlled. The D0 performance morphology was obtained by defect monitoring throughout whole process cycle with use of metrology tool particles scanned. In summary, this work demonstrated that the high temperature ammonia purge significantly enhanced the D0 performance of LPCVD Nitride process. The result showed that the average defect counts were reduced effectively by 92% from previous high defectivity after ammonia purge conditioning. Process cycles cumulative thickness prolonged by 29% from initial maximum cumulative thickness target set. Preventive maintenance activity conducted frequency was reduced by 31%.

articleTitle: A New and Innovative In situ Plasma Etch Pin-up Clean for Defect Reduction and Process Simplification
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Removal of carbon-based polymer on the wafer edge bevel frontside and backside has attracted more attention in an attempt to reduce defects and improve yield. In this paper, we demonstrate a new and innovative plasma pin-up clean method to in situ remove polymers from both the wafer backside and the edge bevel areas. The results from real production wafers show the pin-up clean step can eliminate the carbon-based polymer at both frontside and backside of wafer bevel areas. This pin-up clean concept has been applied to multiple layers in various plasma etch tools for bevel dry etch step elimination and defect reduction with substantial yield improvement. We present the results of two cases that we apply the pin-up clean to remove flake defects and eliminate a down-stream bevel dry etch process step.

articleTitle: From Variations to Precision: Modeling and Optimization of Inner Spacer Etch in GAA FETs
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work introduces a robust machine learning framework for modeling and optimizing the inner spacer etch process in gate-all-around FET fabrication. Using an in-house Particle Monte-Carlo simulator, the etch process is modeled precisely across varied conditions. Gaussian Process Regression outperforms neural network models, achieving 98-99% accuracy in predicting etch front variations. Bayesian Optimization with adaptive sampling and successive domain reduction is utilized to fine-tune etch parameters, minimizing the error between predicted and target etch fronts. This integrated approach enables precise control over spacer-channel geometry, making this approach highly effective for advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Radially Spreading Micro-Bubble Defect due to Contamination from SEM
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: An investigation into the origin and control strategies for a distinct defect characterized by radially spreading wafer maps was conducted during the spin-on hard-mask (SOH), photo resist (PR), and spin-on dielectric (SOD) coating processes. It was found that this defect is closely associated with wafer review or critical dimension (CD) measurements using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) prior to the coating process, and exists in the form of micro-bubbles. To determine the formation mechanism, surface contamination analysis, contact angle, and potential measurements were performed. The results indicated a mechanism for bubble formation resulting from locally inhomogeneous wafer surface hydrophobization caused by carbon compound-based contamination in a vacuum SEM chamber, leading to bubble nucleation and air entrapment during the acceleration coating stage. As preventive measures, the organic contamination source was reduced by cleaning the SEM chamber, and it was demonstrated that implementing enhanced reducing resist consumption (RRC) in the photo process and treatments such as pre-wet cleaning or O2 plasma ashing are effective solutions.

articleTitle: A novel statechart modeling language adapted to R&D automation development : Topic: FA: Factory Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper focuses on a novel Harel statechart modeling language adapted to automation development in a Research and Development (R&D) environment. R&D facilities are characterized by a large variety of tools and specific needs when it comes to automation deployment. In particular, the fine tool behavioral modeling requested is leading to the need for a specific statechart modeling language (SML). The SML language definition will be detailed. The implementation of the language, and the application of this language during automation development and deployment in an R&D shop floor will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Particle Control for Low-Energy Boron Implantation : CFM: Contamination-Free Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We present a case study describing how particles added to wafers during dedicated low-energy boron (LEB) implants can be reduced by the implementation of new hardware to reduce the buildup of boron films on beamline components. The new hardware increases the ion beam angle of incidence on beamline component surfaces to enhance self-sputtering of films and significantly reduces the film growth rate on surfaces near the wafer being implanted. This is important because film growth can lead to delamination which is a particle source. Particle adders can reduce device yields.

articleTitle: Human WIP Delivery in a Manual Fab
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Human work in progress (WIP) delivery in a manual fab is a case study to reduce waiting waste by implementing a dedicated transporter of WIP in a manual 300mm semiconductor fab setting. All waiting waste reduction is valuable in research/manufacturing because it reduces cycle time, alleviates WIP starvation at downstream tools, and increases utilization of the tool family. An experiment was done to test the impact of having a person solely responsible for delivering WIP to the tool. While utilization did not improve as expected, tool throughput was improved in relation to the WIP starvation level during the timeframe of the experiment.

articleTitle: An Industry Plan for Cybersecurity : IE: Industrial Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor factories are high value targets for cyberattacks. Protecting factories is challenging: the complex chip manufacturing process requires a web of third-party equipment, computer devices, and software – any one of which could expose a vulnerability that hackers can exploit. This paper explores the collaborative efforts of industry players to develop greater security through cooperation.

articleTitle: Interaction Study of DIW on Fluoride-Based Solvent Chemical Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the interaction between two key components of Fluoride-Based Solvent: Component A (Fluorine-based, denote as XF) and Deionized Water (DIW), which work in tandem to effectively remove dielectric and metallic polymer residues. However, an undesirable phenomenon observed with the Fluoride-Based Solvent is the excessive increase in metallic and dielectric film loss with usage. This was found to be linked to the depletion of DIW, which results in a more concentrated XF. This paper presents a detailed explanation of the chemical reactions involved in the process and explores potential factors impacting the polymer removal performance. A novel approach is introduced to regulate the DIW concentration through a DIW spiking system with real-time chemical assay analysis. A consistent removal rate performance is achieved, enabling chemical life extension and extended benefits such as improved uptime, cost and quality.

articleTitle: Rapid Probe Microscope (RPM) Technology Advances High-Speed AFM Systems for Next-Generation Semiconductor Metrology
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: High-speed AFM systems for in-line semiconductor process control have recently been commercialised, and this emerging technology is now being integrated into advanced device manufacturing. This paper explores the applications and opportunities of these systems in supporting next-generation metrology and process control, focusing on measurement, data analysis, and achievable throughput under production conditions. Performance data from the Metron3D system is provided, highlighting its use in next-generation lithography and advanced packaging case studies.With the advent of High Numerical Aperture Extreme Ultraviolet (HNA-EUV) lithography, the reduction in lithographic depth of focus necessitates near-perfect planarization across varying lateral scales. For lithographic process optimisation, accumulating evidence demonstrates that 3D Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) metrology provides critical data for the fine-tuning of these processes, offering localised 3D insights that are unattainable with current electron beam (e-beam) and optical metrology methods. The Rapid Probe Microscope (RPM), an advanced hybrid optical AFM incorporated into the Metron3D system is evaluated. The RPM’s sensitivity to lithographic process parameters is demonstrated through 3D characterisation of contact hole geometries at feature sizes smaller than current technology nodes, achieving critical dimensions (CD) down to 12 nm, aligning with the stringent requirements of HNA-EUV lithography.The advancing demands of next-generation packaging technologies impose equally rigorous performance standards on Chemical Mechanical Planarisation (CMP) processes. For advanced packaging, particularly in hybrid bonding processes, A robust methodology for measuring copper pad heights on semiconductor wafers is presented, at a scanning speed of 7.1 mm/s, with exceptional repeatability of 20 pm, whilst achieving throughput rates exceeding 60 wafers per hour (WPH) under standard sampling conditions for in – line use.Significant progress has also been made in advanced image processing algorithms and integrated data analysis, enabling capabilities such as image segmentation, pattern recognition, dimensional analysis, and detection of nuanced metrology signals, further enhancing the precision and utility of RPM in semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Using Machine Vision for Fault Detection of Dry Resist Top Film Peeling : Topic/category: Advanced Process Control
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: While peeling the polyethylene film off a dry film resist, a common fault is that the film tears and some of the film remains on the wafer. Such a fault is often not identified by existing tool sensors so that costly and time-consuming visual verification and/or macro-inspection metrology must be used. This paper discusses a fault detection approach which uses a low-cost video stream along with machine vision technology to identify peeler faults. Furthermore, machine vision is used to infer tool events so that process sensorization and robust fault detection is possible without extensive and risky equipment integration.

articleTitle: Enhanced Annealing and Material with Crystal Originated Particles for Localized Yield Improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: High temperature annealing is widely applied to repair implantation damage in high voltage Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) devices. However, the boat pin contact region often experiences plastic deformation under such aggressive thermal conditions. In this paper, we demonstrate an optimized furnace annealing process designed to enhance Bulk Microdefects (BMDs) formation, combined with Crystal Originated Particles (COPs) in the silicon substrate, to improve the wafer mechanical strength. The optimized condition achieves a 90% reduction of 4-pin defect depth, significantly minimizing wafer deformation and enhancing yield performance.

articleTitle: Implementation & Application of coherent control systems: Digital Twin (high frequency open loop) with R2R (low frequency closed loop)
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A Digital Twin (Applied Twin™) is a computational model that represents a physical asset such as a process chamber, evolving over time to reflect its structure, behavior, and context. This model treats the asset-twin system as a set of coupled dynamical systems that evolve over time, interacting through observed data and control inputs. [1] They are an evolution of modeling & simulation. The Digital Twin (DT) can be useful in integration, testing, monitoring, and maintenance. Eventually it can be utilized as an early and ad hoc fast learning tool for systems and processes. In semiconductor manufacturing, DTs have found their way in their early rudimentary form as control or predictive applications such as for production control applications like planning, scheduling, and dispatching and for equipment and process control applications like, Run-to-Run (Applied SmartFactory™ Run-2-Run) (R2R), Virtual Metrology, and predictive maintenance. Through this paper we explore the idea of idea of engineering DT and R2R algorithms with intersecting system manipulated variables or inputs between the two systems.

articleTitle: SiGe Base Engineering in HBTs for Improving Breakdown and ICES Leakage Characteristics : YE: Yield Enhancement/ Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Silicon-germanium (SiGe) heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) enabled reduced base widths and increased base doping due to bandgap engineering of the SiGe base. However, the base width is constrained by punch-through breakdown. The incorporation of SiGe with silicon forms a heterojunction, introducing strain into the SiGe or Si during fabrication. Fully strained SiGe layers are typically stable and free of dislocations post-growth. It is essential to produce high quality, strained SiGe base layers, as the carrier mobility in these layers is significantly enhanced compared to Si BJTs. However, a relaxed SiGe base layer is undesirable due to the presence of misfit dislocations, which act as generation-recombination centers, degrading leakage current performance. This paper outlines a strategy for improving breakdown voltage and ICES leakage characteristics in SiGe HBTs by optimizing the SiGe base dopant profile, thickness, and growth rate throughout the fabrication process.

articleTitle: Sustainable Piranha Acid Management and Reuse via Redox-Active Catalytic Media
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, piranha acid, a mixture of sulfuric acid and hydrogen peroxide, is commonly used to clean silicon wafers but poses significant disposal challenges due to its hazardous nature. Current disposal methods, such as off-site transport or hydrochloric acid addition, are expensive, risky, and generate additional hazardous byproducts. This study introduces a novel redox-active catalytic media that efficiently decomposes hydrogen peroxide in piranha acid on-site, converting it to water and oxygen. This approach reduces environmental risks, simplifies the disposal process, and aligns with industry goals for safety and sustainability.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Optimize Asymmetric NMOS Device Performance without Impacting the Main Device Functionality
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The continuous drive for scaling and its associated challenges like short channel effects on one hand, the quest for high drive current and requirements of high voltage applications on other hand, give rise to newer device architecture like asymmetric LDD NMOS devices. When both the main device and the asymmetric slave devices are present on same integrated circuit, independent process tuning for each device is not normally possible as they share same set of masks and process steps. In this paper, we studied the sensitivity of each process to main and asymmetric devices, and we propose, for the first time, a methodology to independently adjust the asymmetric NMOS device performance without impacting the main devices. By inserting a N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma surface treatment after the LDD/pocket implant, the behavior of asymmetric NMOS can be modified with little effect on standard NMOS. The N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> treatment after the LDD implant believed to alter the dopant profile near to the pocket region and determines the threshold voltage. No electrical or reliability degradation is observed with the introduction of forming gas treatment. No such study was published before and the study from this paper provides new degree of freedom to process engineers to optimize the processes to achieve both main and asymmetric device specification requirements.

articleTitle: Mathematical and Simulation-Based Analysis of Multiple-Load Mobile Transport Systems in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the semiconductor manufacturing processes, single-load mobile transport systems, which can handle only one load at a time, have traditionally been employed. However, with the increasing demand for transport efficiency, the adoption of multiple-load mobile transport systems has been expanding. This study aims to systematically analyze the multiple-load mobile transport system by implementing an algorithm that determines optimal decisions dynamically at each job request, enabling the identification of policy-independent characteristics of the system. Through mathematical analysis in static problem instances, this study identifies key factors influencing the operational efficiency of multiple-load mobile transport systems. Furthermore, it evaluated whether these factors exhibit consistent tendencies in dynamic environments by utilizing the implemented algorithm and a simulation environment replicating semiconductor manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: A CNN-Based Model for Yield Prediction in MEMS Resonator Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work presents a novel method for predicting the yield of Micro-electromechanical Systems (MEMS) resonators by using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract morphological features from cross-sections images of MEMS resonators’ beams produced by Deep Reactive-Ion Etching (DRIE). By establishing a model that maps the relationships between the MEMS resonators’ operating frequency and the morphological variations in beams induced by process deviations, this method can predict the operating frequency more than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> times faster than Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation, achieving over 96.7% accuracy, advancing the standardization of MEMS resonators manufacturing flow.

articleTitle: High aspect ratio container edge profile tilting solution on advanced DRAM technology
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We introduce a comprehensive solution to the High Aspect Ratio Container (HARC) dry etch process for the 1-beta DRAM process, achieving a sustainable, high-efficiency, and production-friendly solution. This method results in a 37% gain in Mean Time Between Clean (MTBC) and a 2.3% increase in etch chamber availability, leading to a 0.3% yield improvement. The solution includes a control method using adjustable edge RF (Radio Frequency) forward power to manage plasma drift in the chamber, and compensate edge ring height change to prevent plasma sheath distortion caused by edge ring erosion. This control method can be implemented in more advanced HARC plasma etch processes (1-gamma process) to enhance the performance.

articleTitle: Controlling Physical and Electrical Properties of Polysilicon
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Polysilicon is widely used in semiconductor technologies for forming gate electrodes in MOS devices, precision electrical resistors, and waveguides in optical devices. The properties of deposited polysilicon are generally predictable and stable, allowing us to control only the height and width of polysilicon structures using inline measurements to ensure the desired electrical properties. However, in some cases, height and width measurements alone are not sufficient to ensure the proper electrical properties, particularly electrical resistance. To achieve the target electrical resistance in polysilicon with specific physical dimension, it is crucial to control the grain size. We demonstrate a simple in-line inspection method for grain size and propose an effective control method for mass production, utilizing Auto Machine Learning(AutoML)

articleTitle: Study of As-Deposited and Annealed Atomic Layer Deposited Hafnium Silicate Films
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this study, we are depositing hafnium silicate films using Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) technique with hafnium tetrachloride (HfCl4) and silicon tetrachloride (SiCl4) as precursor and water (H2O) as oxidant. We are analyzing impact of variation in number of ALD cycles on film thickness. We are also studying the impact of SiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> vessel temperature and chamber susceptor temperature on hafnium silicate film thickness. The hafnium silicate films were sent to Decoupled Plasma Nitridation (DPN) chamber to form HfSiON followed by Post Nitridation Annealing (PNA) to observe the effect on thickness, Hf-concentration, SiO-bond percentage, N concentration, and O concentration with variation in post nitridation anneal temperature and pressure. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profile data was obtained for annealed and unannealed films. These process parameter modulations help in better understanding of the reaction mechanisms in ALD and PNA.

articleTitle: Yield Loss Due to the Interaction Between Dissolved Oxygen in DI Water and Megasonic in Final Rinse Process
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This proposed paper presents an intriguing case study on yield loss investigation and failure mechanisms in semiconductor manufacturing. This study is significant because it uncovers a failure mode that is not typically anticipated, providing valuable insights for selecting cleaning process recipes, especially for smaller features. In semiconductor manufacturing, maintaining lower dissolved oxygen (DO) levels in deionized water (DIW) is essential to eliminate charging and contamination-related failures. Similarly, the application of megasonic power in wet cleaning recipes is generally employed to achieve better cleaning and higher yield. However, these practices may not be advantageous in all scenarios, particularly when interacting with smaller geometries. We present a yield loss mechanism resulting from the interaction between lower DO levels in DIW and megasonic cleaning in RCA processes. This interaction can lead to significant failures, particularly in smaller emitter cavities, where the effects of surface tension and capillary forces become more pronounced. The findings from this study are essential for enhancing the reliability and yield of semiconductor devices. Implementing strategies to control DO levels and megasonic treatment parameters can significantly improve the effectiveness of the cleaning process and ensure the quality of the manufactured products.

articleTitle: Wafer-Less Warm-up and Ramp-up Time Optimization for CMP Cost and Wastage Reduction : MS: Manufacturing for Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The use of warm-up wafers in Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) processes represents a significant source of operational costs and inefficiencies in semiconductor manufacturing. Conventionally, 4 to 8 dummy wafers are utilized during the warm-up phase to condition polishing pads and stabilize slurry systems, ensuring optimal tool performance after maintenance or technology node transitions. However, as semiconductor technologies advance, featuring increasingly complex multi-layer architectures and intricate CMP steps, the reliance on dummy wafers has led to escalating operational costs, heightened resource consumption, and environmental concerns [1]. In response, this paper presents a novel Wafer-less Warm-up (WLWU) method that eliminates the need for dummy wafers by leveraging advanced pad conditioning techniques. WLWU simulates the effects of traditional warm-up processes by refreshing the polishing pad surface and optimizing slurry flow rates, ensuring production-ready conditions without compromising pad lifespan or process stability. Rigorous testing across various CMP process steps and toolsets demonstrates that WLWU can be effectively implemented without introducing inline variation or negatively impacting production yield. The findings underscore WLWU as a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable alternative to traditional warm-up procedures. By reducing dummy wafer usage, WLWU offers the semiconductor industry significant operational savings, potentially amounting to hundreds of millions of dollars annually. Additionally, it aligns with broader sustainability initiatives by minimizing material waste and resource consumption. This study highlights WLWU’s transformative potential, positioning it as a viable solution for enhancing efficiency and sustainability in CMP wafer fabrication.

Author Keywords: Process of Record (POR) Semiconductor Climate Consortium (SCC)

articleTitle: Inline Defect and Logic and Memory Diagnostic Net Path Overlap Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Inline inspections on advanced nodes always face challenges in terms of sensitivity and nuisance rates. It is difficult to optimize inspection recipes and efficiently check results for strong yield correlation. Engineers need to obtain inspection results with defect images and classifications, then compare these with yield data for optimization [1], [2], [3]. Here we demonstrate an accurate method for setting up inspection areas and reviewing the relationship between defects and fail bins by overlapping defect locations and fail net paths. Inspection areas can be defined by High Volume Diagnostic fail net path and implemented in inspection equipment. We can overlap defect locations with diagnostic fail net paths to evaluate the hit rate of the captured defect. This method can assist defect engineers in setting up high sensitivity and low nuisance recipes easily, help optimally utilize FA resources and support product engineers in finding more accurate directions to improve yield. Overall, advanced manufacturing fabs can implement this method to achieve higher yields quickly.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-Variate Anomaly Detection Method For Chemical Vapor Deposition
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Current method of anomaly detection is typically univariate SPC control which false alarm increases proportionally with number of parameters (high dimensional). New anomaly detection methods (ABOD and LOF) were applied to address high-dimensional issues in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) high density plasma oxide (HDPO) for 20 days, but the initial false alarm rate was still 65.6%. Further improvement was achieved in reducing false alarms by applying supervised machine learning approach, which is random forest, on the same tool set, and tested the model against data obtained. The false alarm rate was further down 8.7%, representing a 7.5 times reduction in false alarm rate based on the supervised machine learning model and annotation by module engineering to identify genuine outlier cases.

articleTitle: Reducing Wafer Scraps with AI: Detecting Hidden Damage in Vacuum Chambers
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, damage to certain parts of a vacuum chamber often goes undetected until the chamber is physically inspected or a defect map from processed wafers is obtained. This study proposes a machine learning (ML) based approach to analyze multivariate sensor data and detect hidden chamber damage in real time. By combining unsupervised and supervised learning models, the methodology demonstrated strong predictive capabilities in identifying key indicators of part damage. This approach enhances fault detection capabilities, reduces maintenance time, and prevents wafer losses. The findings highlight the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven analytics in improving predictive maintenance and optimizing semiconductor manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: A Perspective on Interconnect Scaling Challenges in the NanoStack Transistor Era : AP/DFM: Advanced Patterning / Design for Manufacturing (Design-Technology Co-Optimization)
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper explores various design and technology co-optimization (DTCO) challenges as they apply to back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnects used for vertically-stacked Nanosheet ("NanoStack") transistor architectures. Aggressive interconnect pitch scaling may drive the industry toward direct-etch patterning of lines with embedded air gaps, which pose challenges in terms of process integration as well as variability. Backside power delivery network (BSPDN) architectures remove power rails from frontside interconnect track plans but pose stringent requirements on ground rules (such as tip-to-end and via enclosures) which may require cut patterning. Certain architectures, such as NanoStack transistors and/or skip-level interconnect vias, require extreme high aspect ratio etch and metallization with extreme resistance sensitivity to post-metallization vertical profile. Looking to the future, new classes of materials have been identified which possess fundamentally different resistivity scaling mechanisms than conventional metals, though the CMOS-compatible integration of these materials remains a question. These challenges and more are discussed in the context of advanced interconnects for optimized power, performance, area and cost (PPAC) in next-generation semiconductor technologies.

articleTitle: Compositional Analysis of Thick Silicon Nitride Films Using X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents inline and offline X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) data of thick SiN films prepared by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) and low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) techniques. The inline XPS monitors the stoichiometry of the film surface, while offline XPS is used to understand the entire thick film composition and Si/SiNx interface. For a complete compositional analysis, the XPS depth profile and detailed core-level spectra analysis are conducted for annealed and unannealed wafers. Finally, the XPS thickness is confirmed from cross-section images.

articleTitle: Understanding the Mechanism of Metal Oxide Defect Formation at the Via Bottom
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The semiconductor manufacturing process is a complex and intricate system that is susceptible to even the slightest deviations. Yield issues can significantly affect production efficiency and product reliability. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the intertwined technical and systemic factors involved is essential for maintaining high yield rates in semiconductor manufacturing. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of a recurring yield issue, illustrating how various factors can converge to compromise yield for the borderless or zero enclosure Via* design. The proposed yield loss mechanism, a key contribution of this analysis, was validated, paving the way for its practical application in selecting wet cleaning chemicals for the post Via* etch residual removal for tight Via* overlay designs.

articleTitle: Semiconductor SEM Image Defect Classification Using Supervised and Semi-Supervised Learning with Vision Transformers : Topic/category: Defect Inspection and Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Controlling defects in semiconductor processes is important for maintaining yield, improving production cost, and preventing time-dependent critical component failures. Electron beam-based imaging has been used as a tool to survey wafers in the line and inspect for defects. However, manual classification of images for these nano-scale defects is limited by time, labor constraints, and human biases. In recent years, deep learning computer vision algorithms have shown to be effective solutions for image-based inspection applications in industry. This work proposes application of vision transformer (ViT) neural networks for automatic defect classification (ADC) of scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of wafer defects. We evaluated our proposed methods on 300mm wafer semiconductor defect data from our fab in IBM Albany. We studied 11 defect types from over 7400 total images and investigated the potential of transfer learning of DinoV2 and semi-supervised learning for improved classification accuracy and efficient computation. We were able to achieve classification accuracies of over 90% with less than 15 images per defect class. Our work demonstrates the potential to apply the proposed framework for a platform agnostic in-house classification tool with faster turnaround time and flexibility.

articleTitle: Correlation Between In-Situ Wafer-Level Temperature Distribution During the Etch Process and Via Resistivity
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Creating vias and lines in semiconductor manufacturing demands high precision in both the lateral and depth dimensions of etched structures. When etching through the dielectric layer, it is crucial to reach the metallic contact beneath to ensure optimal electrical performance and reliability. Vias with low resistivity minimize energy loss, current dissipation, and heat generation. The cross-wafer uniformity of via resistivity is a key performance indicator for the chip manufacturing process. Identifying any non-uniformity and linking it to controllable parameters of an etch process chamber – such as electrostatic chuck temperature, exclusion ring temperature, and plasma-on properties – enables optimal tuning of the etch process and enhances yield. This is especially important during the R&D phase to ensure optimal yield in subsequent pilot line and high-volume chip manufacturing phases.In this study, we employed a wireless in-situ temperature sensor wafer to investigate the origin of a high via resistivity region within the wafer. Using production recipe conditions, we discovered a strong correlation between wafer-level temperature distribution and in-line vias resistivity results. Additionally, we used the temperature measurement wafer to assess the impact of electrostatic chuck temperature, edge ring temperature, and plasma-on properties on wafer-level temperature. These findings offer valuable insights into the performance of the dielectric plasma etch processes and equipment, enabling process development, optimization, chamber matching and improved high-volume manufacturing process monitoring.

articleTitle: Defectivity in Silicon Nitride Etching with Phosphoric Acid using Single Wafer Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Single wafer cleaning processing can effectively address particle and defect issues commonly associated with conventional batch processing. However, phosphoric acid wet etching of silicon nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) continues to rely on batch processing in semiconductor manufacturing. In this work, we assess single wafer processing for phosphoric acid etching, focusing on improved uniformity and defect reduction. We demonstrate that single wafer processing achieves within-wafer uniformity of less than 5 % at a high silicon nitride etching thickness of 600 Å. We discuss how defectivity increases with queue time and highlight the importance of optimizing rinsing steps for reducing defects.

articleTitle: CD-SEM Anomaly Detection Through Machine Learning and Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In a complex semiconductor manufacturing environment, critical dimension scanning electron microscope (CD-SEM) images are captured at metrology step to monitor structural measurements and detect anomaly to meet the stringent process control requirements. This paper focuses on advanced CD-SEM image processing and anomaly detection using machine learning and generative AI models, which include computer vision (CV) image processing, Residual Neural Network (ResNet) deep learning and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) model for various use cases. The applications of these models during in-line monitoring are crucial to identify potential process issues for yield and quality improvement.

articleTitle: Impact of Rapid Thermal Process on Lithography Overlay
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The influence of rapid thermal processing parameters such as temperature offset on lithography overlay were investigated. The substrate quality is another critical factor that can affect overlay residue. Optimized temperature offset on the wafers edge is applied depending on substrate for overlay improvement. In addition, wafer centering inside the chamber played a critical role causing wafer warpage, ending up with overlay residue issue.

articleTitle: Measuring Key Parameters (Depth and Bottom CD) in Deep Trench Isolation Applications (>50 μm) with the New SpectraShape™
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Measuring non-destructive deep trenches, through silicon vias (TSV), and structures having high aspect ratio and large pitch applications is becoming important in today’s semiconductor industry (e.g., hybrid bonding, power technologies, etc.). [1], [2] Effective monitoring of critical parameters inline is crucial to establish and maintain stable device performance and guaranteeing high yield. In this paper, we will show the possibility to measure deep trenches using the new designed SpectraShape™ dimensional metrology system.
