articleTitle: A New Continuous Plasma Process For Defect Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In a DRAM polysilicon etch back process, blocked etch defects existed in the high-volume manufacturing (HVM) production line, resulting in low chamber uptime, yield loss and reliability issue. In this paper, we present our results from a newly developed continuous plasma process (CPP) together with higher TCP power defume for defect reduction. With the implementation of this new CPP recipe, we have achieved 0.1% yield gain from defect reduction and ~25% RPT reduction.

articleTitle: Gas Phase Nucleation Detection Using Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: LAM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> Altus Tungsten chemical vapor deposition (WCVD) process needs to monitor gas phase nucleation (GPN) as one of process control parameters. Main factor causing GPN is the increased in silane (SiH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) flow (relative to WF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> flow), which create W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> particles. The GPN, which occurs during production, will lead to tungsten void due to SiH4 burst in nucleation step. However, control for such critical parameters is still manually done by visual inspection on a weekly basis. Hence, the auto GPN detection has been implemented using image recognition that is able to reduce human error and misjudgment, which in turn prevent wafer scraps incidents.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Defect Detection using Deep Learning: A Pattern-Agnostic Faster R-CNN Approach for SEM Images with GPU Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing requires highly precise defect detection to ensure product quality and yield. This paper presents a deep learning-based defect detection framework using Faster R-CNN to identify and classify defects in Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images, specifically within the modeling flow, which is used to simulate and predict semiconductor process behavior based on metrology data. The process begins with manufacturing test patterns through the photolithography process, followed by metrology analysis using a SEM machine. If a defect is present in the SEM image, the associated metrology data may become unreliable, potentially degrading the accuracy of the simulation models built on this data. Using such erroneous data in model creation could lead to inaccurate predictions and weaker models.To address this issue, our method filters out defective data, ensuring that only high-quality, defect-free measurements contribute to model development. This leads to more reliable semiconductor process simulations and improved process decisions. Leveraging the proven performance of Faster R-CNN—particularly its effectiveness in detecting small, low-contrast anomalies—the model generalizes across diverse layouts without requiring pattern-specific training. It achieves a mAP of 83% at IoU = 0.5, significantly reducing manual inspection time and improving defect classification accuracy. Our approach enables scalable, automated inspection of SEM data, enhancing the overall efficiency, robustness, and precision of the semiconductor modeling and manufacturing pipeline.

articleTitle: Eliminating Half Wafer Shading Defects in Lithography Track Tools using Open Shutter Method
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss how we addressed an increase in defectivity in our lithography track tools, specifically the half wafer shading (HWS) defect. This defect signature appears as a concentration of particles on half of the wafer and was correlated to an airflow issue in the bake units making it more susceptible to particle contaminants from the external environment. Using a simple modification of the hardware functionality by permanently opening the bake unit shutter, we were able to resolve the HWS defect signature. A mist test was done to validate the open shutter method and CFD simulation was used to understand the failure mechanism. With this method, we eliminated the HWS defect on product wafers.

articleTitle: Thermodynamics of phase separation in SiGe solid solution and construction of the miscibility gap at low temperatures for cubic-phase Si-Ge binary alloy semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The subject paper presents a thermodynamic study of the low-temperature spinodal decomposition in SiGe solid solutions and its impact on the properties and performance of Si-Ge alloy semiconductors. The miscibility gap in SiGe alloys originates from their positive enthalpy of mixing and has implications on their bandgap, charge carrier mobility, thermal conductivity and optoelectronic properties. In this study, we have calculated the enthalpy of mixing of Si-Ge alloy system using DFT and based on our results, we were able to construct a low-temperature phase diagram and identify the unstable and metastable regions of the spinodal plot and also identify the different thermodynamic and kinetic factors that govern the formation of these phase-separated regions.

articleTitle: Process-Aware Digital Twins for Nanofabrication Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Digital twins are computer representations of the structure, context, and behavior of a physical system; for example, nanofabrication cleanroom process equipment such as a DUV stepper or plasma etcher. For process equipment where the input and output can be described by images, such as optical or SEM images, this paper proposes HyperPix2Pix, a deep neural network that can be trained to represent a variety of equipment, including the effects of process parameters. In this paper, we demonstrate HyperPix2Pix on DUV photolithography and plasma etch tools. Compared to previous work, HyperPix2Pix introduces structured process parameters through multimodal learning that elucidates the role of different parameters in nanofabrication processes.

articleTitle: WEE Residue Elimination for Cross-Link Prone Positive Tone DUV Photoresists
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In DUV lithography process, some positive tone photoresists (PR) exhibit negative tone PR characteristics under certain exposure and baking process conditions. Such cross-link reactions cause PR residue on the Wafer Edge Exposure (WEE) zone of the wafer, which becomes a source of defects in downstream manufacturing steps, affecting the electrical performance and yield of products. This paper explores the effects of WEE illumination, post-exposure bake, and developing time on the formation of WEE PR residue. It was found that post-exposure bake temperature had the largest impact on the elimination of WEE residue while WEE illumination and developing time played smaller roles.

articleTitle: A Study on Barc Endpoint Profile Transformation Caused by Different Metal/Via Reticle Transmission Ratio in Oxide trench Etch Processes : APC: Advanced Process Control
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach of using the Reticle Transmission (RT) ratio of Via and metal to understand the endpoint profile of a BARC/Silicon Nitride (Nitride) etch. This study was conducted on Via first dual damascene process which uses an endpoint method to control the BARC/Nitride etch step. The aim of this study is to use the RT ratio to make predictions on endpoint profile for new products and allow system to select the best recipe. With this new method, it will reduce machine endpoint faults which may arise from products with a wide range of metal and via RT values.

articleTitle: General Framework for Processing Time Prediction and Machine Availability for all Fab Equipment
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach that significantly improves processing time (PT) and machine availability predictions across all tools in a GlobalFoundries semiconductor fabrication plant. An attention-based deep neural network was developed to enhance prediction accuracy. The model achieved a 50% to 80% reduction in Mean Absolute Error for PT and machine availability predictions, compared to a baseline statistical model. Deployment on three bottleneck tool families led to a 3% to 7% improvement in chamber utilization. The model is being expanded to all GlobalFoundries' facilities, with expected similar outcomes.

articleTitle: Novel Placement of Overlay Marks to Eliminate Measurement Errors for Thick Photoresist Layers
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Thick photoresists (PRs) are often used in mature tech nodes for high-dose or high-energy ion implant steps that form the deep well implants required for device isolation. The overlay control of such layers is critical in determining the channel length of the transistor. However, the PR profile of the overlay marks is prone to directional overcuts, depending on the mark’s proximity to large, exposed patterns nearby. These overcut profiles lead to erroneous overlay measurements that compromise the integrity of the feedback to Lithography’s run-to-run Advanced Process Control. This paper explores various placements of overlay marks as a solution to reduce or eliminate such overcuts and ensure maximum overlay fidelity is achieved. By placing the overlay marks at select scribe lane junctions within the reticle field, the true overlay can be measured and controlled, enabling stable electrical performance of devices.

articleTitle: Optimizing PMOS performance: Enhancing PLDD Implantation by switching from Boron to BF2
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In most submicron processes, the p-type lightly doped drain (PLDD) implant is typically performed using a low-energy boron (B) implant, as low as 0.6 keV. Boron, being a light atom, is easily accelerated in the ion beam, resulting in a high projected range and straggle. To achieve the desired implantation profile, a lower energy implant is performed in a deceleration mode, which presents challenges in dose repeatability and energy contamination. These challenges can lead to inconsistencies in device performance, particularly in the PMOS Idsat electrical test (ET) parameter, which may fall out-of-specification (OOS), resulting in low yield, wafer scrap, and higher costs. To address these issues, this study explores the conversion from boron(B) to boron difluoride (BF2), a heavier atom. The BF2 implant process offers several advantages: improved variations and dose control due to the heavier mass of the BF2 molecule, enhanced tool up time and throughput, increased process margin for ET and yield, and superior reliability performance. BF2 implants reduce boron penetration and mitigate damage, leading to better performance in key reliability tests such as Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI), Hot Carrier Injection (HCI), and Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB). The results indicate that BF2 implants are a preferable choice over boron for advanced semiconductor manufacturing, providing improved process efficiency, yield, and device reliability.

articleTitle: Tool Matching and Process Optimization for Contact Metal CMP Contamination Reduction : CFM: Contamination-Free Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Contamination from a Contact Metal CMP process leads to downstream embedded defects that lead to yield loss and Return Material Authorization (RMA’s) from customers due to fails during end use. This process has a unique cleaning methodology on both the polisher and cleaner side to minimize the formation of embedded defects that cause downstream metal interconnect shorts. Continuous improvements are needed to address the root cause of the failure and prevent defective product from being sent to the customer.

articleTitle: IP-aware Federated Manufacturing Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The application of deep learning in semiconductor manufacturing holds great promise but faces significant challenges, particularly in safeguarding intellectual property (IP) during data exchanges. Consider a scenario where the same equipment is deployed across multiple manufacturers. Equipment providers need to collect operational data to offer continuous service improvements, while manufacturers must balance the utility of shared data with the risk of IP leakage. This challenge is compounded by the opacity of deep learning models, raising the question: how can manufacturers ensure their sensitive data remains protected? We address this issue with the IP-aware Federated Manufacturing Intelligence (IPFMI) framework, a novel distributed learning architecture designed to ensure IP protection in federated learning (FL) settings. In IPFMI, data collected by Remote Equipment (RE) at each Semiconductor Manufacturer (SM) undergoes an IP-preserving transformation before being shared with a centralized Service Architect (SA). The SA aggregates this sanitized data to train a central model, enabling performance improvements such as predictive maintenance, process optimization, and anomaly detection without accessing raw data. This approach strikes a balance between utility and privacy, facilitating secure, privacy-preserving collaboration between manufacturers and equipment providers.

articleTitle: Study of Pre-Amorphization Implant Species Impact on PNP Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Pre-amorphization implant (PAI) is used to prevent channeling and transient enhanced diffusion (TED). High-energy boron collector implants tend to diffuse to the base, causing higher leakages. Several species can be used for PAI, each with its own set of challenges. In this paper, we studied the effects of argon and silicon as PAI in a PNP device. Argon PAI can improve leakage performance but causes a significant decrease in gain due to an increase in base current. Silicon, on the other hand, is the best species for improving leakage by eight orders of magnitude without much degradation in gain. The superior leakage performance provided by silicon PAI makes it a highly reliable choice for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The findings from this study can be applied to other device architectures where PAI is used for performance improvements.

articleTitle: DNN-based Predictive Digital Twin for FHE Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work presents a novel predictive model and a virtual metrology for Flexible and Printable Electronic (FHE) device fabrication using deep learning techniques. Our method leverages the Deep Neural Network (DNN) based model Pix2Pix to predict outcomes of 3D inkjet printing from layout images. We prepared an experimental FHE dataset that captures printed electronics’s intricate patterns and printing process variability. By training the Pix2Pix model on this dataset, we successfully demonstrated its ability to learn and accurately predict the outcome of inkjet printing of structures using a conductive ink. The best mean absolute errors (MAE) for width and gap prediction are 5.07 microns and 7.99 microns. This approach enables improvement of efficiency and accuracy of printed electronics, paving the way for advancements in FHE manufacturing technology and workflows.

articleTitle: Cryogenic Plasma Etching Process Optimization Using a Wireless CryoTemp™ Metrology Wafer
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: To enhance the etch profile fidelity in advanced 3D flash memory, a cryogenic plasma etching process is employed for the channel hole etch layer. Controlling wafer level temperature and cross-wafer uniformity is crucial in this process. KLA’s newly developed, next generation CryoTemp metrology wafer temperature measurement system offers an in-situ metrology solution for optimizing and controlling the cryogenic plasma etching process. This work demonstrates how the new CryoTemp wafer optimizes the cryogenic plasma etching process for a Lam Research etch tool in 3D flash memory manufacturing. The results show that the CryoTemp wafer is sensitive to RF power and backside helium (He) flow rate, and that temperature correlates well with channel hole etch depth. KLA’s new CryoTemp wafer helps to characterize and stabilize the cryogenic etch process, improving the yield for advanced 3D devices.

articleTitle: CMP Process Improvement for Non-uniform Cu/SiO2 Hybrid Bonding Layout
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this work, a 300 mm wafer with Cu pads of 1 μm x 1 μm is used for a hybrid bonding process research. The Cu/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers were planarized by a three-platen CMP process using different types CMP polishing pads for the Cu recess delta and galvanic corrosion study. The Cu recess is a critical parameter in determining whether wafer to wafer (W2W) hybrid bonding is successful and robust. The non-uniform Cu recess is due to the different antenna ratio of the various Cu pads. CMP polishing pads with various hardness such as soft pads (Shore A: 16.8) and hard pads (Shore D: 54.2 to 67) were evaluated for Cu recess delta and galvanic corrosion study to apply to the W2W hybrid bonding process. Cu CMP pad hardness effect is investigated in the galvanic corrosion study, and it significantly improves Cu recess uniformity for non-uniform hybrid bonding layout.

articleTitle: Arc detection algorithm using Photo Multiplier Tubes
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced algorithmic framework for enhanced detection of high-voltage discharge events (arcs) through photomultiplier tube (PMT) signal analysis, demonstrating substantial improvements in critical arc event classification and yield preservation. Arc detection accuracy is paramount for process control and equipment integrity in plasma-based semiconductor manufacturing. This optimization is especially critical as feature densities increase and critical dimensions decrease in advanced node semiconductor fabrication.

articleTitle: Void Defect Improvement with Barrier Metal-Cu Seed and Electroplating Recipes Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor back end of line metallization requires successful integration of barrier metal (BM), copper seed, and copper electroplating, among other processes, in order to carry signals and power to the transistors below. This can be impeded or blocked by voids in the metal lines. This paper reports an investigation into the reduction of voids on a particular high aspect ratio feature through the optimization of the interface barrier metal (BM), copper seed, and copper electroplating conditions. Results show that these optimizations significantly reduced the void count and allowed for a reduced overall resistance of the metal layer, contributing to an increase in wafer yield.

articleTitle: Contribution of Raman Spectroscopy to Strain Metrology in Trench Array Structures : AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is proposed for the high-resolution measurement of strain in microelectronic devices. This structural property, which operates at different scales, can be measured by different techniques, each with specific sensitivities and probe sizes. The interest of Raman spectroscopy lies in its ability to analyze ultra-thin or 3D structures down to less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> in terms of strain with a submicron lateral resolution. In this work, micron scale pillar arrays are investigated. The combination of μ-Raman with profilometric and morphological measurements illustrates its potential as a new in-line technique for the strain metrology.

articleTitle: AI Driven Defect Map Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper describes an AI-driven automated system that leverages Convolutional Neural networks (CNNs) for real-time wafer map defect recognition. The proposed framework integrates data preparation, wafer map image generation, data augmentation, and a CNN-based classification model to identify systematic defect patterns such as line, streak and ring. An interactive user interface (UI) enables engineers to search for similar defect signatures across historical production data, adjust similarity thresholds, and compute hit rates for anomaly detection. InceptionResNetV2 model that achieved 94.5% accuracy on testing data is utilized as the main framework for this study. The system’s scalability in linking defects to assignable causes such as polishing pad hardening or uneven cleaning, helps to enhance process monitoring and yield management. This work bridges the gap between machine learning and practical industrial application by providing a solution for semiconductor manufacturing challenges.

articleTitle: Device Optimization to Enable Ultra Low Leakage Logic FinFETs
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Leakage reduction is a key consideration for modern chip design as transistors continue to shrink in size to improve power efficiency in integrated circuits. In this paper, we present techniques used to develop ultra-low leakage (ULL) logic FET and SRAM on GlobalFoundries 12LP+ CMOS technology. We will show how junction and gate engineering can lead to ~11x/7x reduction in NFET/PFET devices leakage by keeping the technology on the ring oscillator (RO) performance trend. We will also present more than 10x decrease in static random-access memory (SRAM) leakage during data-retention mode with no degradation on threshold voltage mismatch.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Marker Structure for Precise Electron Probe Positioning and Displacement Measurement in Secondary Electron Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Electron beam lithography requires exceptionally high positioning accuracy for the electron probe to ensure precise patterning. Nevertheless, distortions caused by wafer stage movements and floor vibrations can significantly degrade the high positional accuracy required for precise patterning. Several approaches have been proposed to mitigate the impact of probe vibrations on positioning accuracy, with rubber and pneumatic dampers being standard solutions. In this paper, we measure the electron probe displacement using the microscopic image of a circuit pattern obtained through lithography testing and introduce an innovative electron probe marker region with orthogonal line sets for precise positioning. The proposed pattern consists of two sets of continuous lines, each being orthogonal to the other. These two sets are spaced at different intervals along the scanning line, enabling the separation of the secondary electron-based video signal obtained from scanning the marker pattern into two distinct periodic signals, each corresponding to one of the line sets. We can accurately and rapidly compute the electron probe displacements in two dimensions by applying the Fourier decomposition or the Recursive Least Square method to the video signal by scanning. This displacement estimation can be used to calculate the input voltage of the scan coil of the control system to counteract the vibration. The simulation is processed in MATLAB. The results show that the RMS errors of the calculated probe displacement remain under 4.2 nm by Fourier decomposition and 2.6 nm by the Recursive Least Square method, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed marker pattern.

articleTitle: Purion vs Paradigm Process Matching: Copy Exact Process or Copy Exact Output? : AEPM: Advanced Equipment Processes and Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: As semiconductor manufacturing equipment continues to evolve, with newer model tools offering better process accuracy and precision, semiconductor fabs face the challenge of matching the processes that run on older machines (tools of record) with the same processes set up on newer style equipment. This is a case where copy exact process methodology does not work across vastly different platforms, and a copy exact output approach is needed. For Ion Implantation processes, it is particularly difficult to match the process output of batch machines to that of single-wafer tools. Variations in the implant angle set-up, beamline design, and handling mechanisms across implanter platforms create a nearly impossible task of matching the process exactly. While tight timelines for cross-fab technology transfers demand, in so far as possible, a copy-exact approach, device sensitivities can drive parametric shifts which highlight even the slightest hardware differences. This study will explore the various process knobs for optimization of a critical transistor gain parameter through a tilt-sensitive implant across several 300mm High Energy implant platforms (Axcelis HE3, Axcelis Paradigm XE, Axcelis Purion XE) and utilizing high precision SIMS analysis in conjunction with electrical test to gauge the device performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Particle Performance in Plasma-Resist-Stripping Machines through Pressure Relief Valve Assembly Relocation
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Pressure relief valve is installed in dry resist-stripping machine to ensure system pressure does not exceed allowable limit to prevent component failures from excessive pressure. Despite its function as a gateway providing protection from machine overpressure, the mechanism of releasing pressure from high-pressure system causes turbulence. In dry resist-stripping machine, the pressure relief valve is located on the process chamber body. This design eventually causes particle contamination to the chamber parts due to the turbulence. This paper will elaborate on the design modification of pressure relief valve in resist stripping machine to improve its particle performance.

articleTitle: WCVD SPRINT Recipe Optimization to Eliminate Abnormal Profile
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: AMAT Centura SPRINT chamber encounters abnormal resistivity (Rs) profile intermittently. This effect is seen even with controlled purge ring kit height which helps to minimize the issue by improving edge gases flow. The recipe parameters were studied and by experimenting with the throttle valve (T/V) step value during one of the process recipe steps it able to observe the difference in RS profile result. The T/V opening step was found to affect the wafer backside pressure chucking and de-chucking condition. The root cause of profile Rs abnormal is stemming from wafer de-chucking caused by big T/V step opening. By implementing new T/V step values it can minimize the de-chucking effect and improve wafer resistivity uniformity.

articleTitle: Characterization of Single Mask MIM capacitor with Copper Damascene Metallization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a cost-effective and manufacturable metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitor structure with Copper (Cu) and Titanium Nitride (TiN) electrodes, designed for 130nm 5-level Cu-metallization technology. Several process parameters were optimized to enhance reliability in Cu BEOL processes, including SiN deposition precursor gas flow, soaking conditions, Cu seed process temperature, Cu annealing, and top plate metal profile. These optimizations resulted in low leakage, high breakdown voltage, with improved MIM TDDB reliability. Our findings demonstrate a promising approach to achieving high-performance MIM capacitors for advanced semiconductor applications.

articleTitle: Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) Epitaxial Growth for Enhanced Device, Yield, and Uniformity
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: SiGe for Source/Drain (S/D) regions has been widely analyzed in FinFET technology. The quality of the SiGe within the S/D of a pFET FinFET determines the devices performance, chip level yield, and the within wafer uniformity (WiW). In this study, two SiGe Epi growth processes are compared. The enhanced process results in improved performance, chip level yield, and uniformity compared to the reference. +5% device performance, +0.25% wafer edge Yield gain, and -10% Freq/-5% Iddq on-chip level uniformity sigma reduction are successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition of Cobalt for Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work describes the various "knobs" that can be used in order to optimize the deposition of cobalt by Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition for applications in microelectronics, using cobaltocene as precursor and ammonia or mixtures of hydrogen and nitrogen as co-reactant, and their effect on the properties of Cobalt layers. In particular, this study analyzes the effects of plasma pressure, plasma chemistry, and DC bias, on the growth rate per cycle, resistivity and crystallinity of the layers. It was observed that higher Nitrogen incorporation on the layers promotes crystallinity, while it also increases the resistivity. To our knowledge, this is the first study of Co PEALD with substrate bias, and the results show lower resistivity and better crystallinity control of Co films

articleTitle: Si -Photonics Waveguide Propagation Loss Improvement Through Process Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In silicon photonics devices, waveguides (WG) with lower propagation loss are always preferred due to their efficiency and performance benefits. One of the primary factors contributing to the overall propagation loss in waveguides is the light scattering caused by the roughness of the waveguide sidewalls. This paper presents an evaluation of various lithography and etch process optimizations aimed at reducing sidewall roughness on a 200mm CMOS-compatible photonics platform. Through these optimizations, we have identified that a significant improvement in waveguide propagation can be achieved by optimizing the lithography Post Exposure Bake (PEB) process. This optimization effectively minimizes sidewall roughness, thereby enhancing the overall performance of the waveguides.

articleTitle: Metal layer oxide void leading to a reliability failure
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper will present a unique oxide void found in Flash memory products where the oxide void is present in between metal layers which does not show any functional issues initially but degrades over time and leads to a reliability failure. This is problematic because the defect is not easily detectable by the inline inspection and cannot be screened by the initial electrical functional test either while it takes time to cause functional issues later. While this paper also touches on the detection and screening of the defect, a careful validation at the process design stage is critical to prevent this type of failure mode.

articleTitle: The Process Challenges from Silicon Rich Polymers: A Case Study on Yield Loss Induced by Consecutive Etch and Stripping Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper discusses a case of random yield loss observed in multiple production lots due to leakage failures. Failure analysis (FA) revealed polysilicon bridging and short circuits caused by poly etch blocking, linked to various etch and strip processes. The issue stemmed from the formation of silicon-rich polymers during hard mask etching and poly etching processes, which were inadequately removed in subsequent plasma and chemical resist stripping processes. These polymers accumulated, causing blocked etch in the later poly etch layer and resulting in leakage failures. The analysis identified differences in equipment and process chemistry as the root cause of the polymer formation and removal inefficiency. Experiments to optimize polymer formation and removal are discussed as a reference to future process improvements and enhance wafer yield.

articleTitle: WCVD Chamber Parts Material Selection To Prolong Wetclean Counter
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Tungsten chemical vapor deposition (WCVD) Remote Plasma Clean (RPC) chamber preventive maintenance (PM) wafer counts restricted by wafer transferring and particles performance. Material selection is crucial to minimize byproduct formation and maintain chamber efficiency. This study evaluates the performance of stainless steel, nickel (Ni), and aluminum (Al) components within the chamber. Stainless steel spring washers lead to iron fluoride and chromium fluoride formation, causing rubbing and vibration that results in mechanical issues. In contrast, nickel washers show reduced byproduct formation under normal conditions, though nickel fluoride (NiF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) was form at elevated temperatures. Aluminum components, protected by a stable oxide layer, remain inert, preventing AlF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> formation and maintaining chamber cleanliness. Further analysis suggests aluminum screws significantly decrease contamination, enhancing process quality and reducing maintenance needs. The transition to nickel washers and aluminum screws optimizes chamber performance, extending operational efficiency and reducing costs.

articleTitle: Lifetime Extension for Oxide Etch Application with Silicon Carbide Focus Ring
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper proposes the change of focus ring (FR) material from silicon (Si) to silicon carbide (SiC) to extend the lifetime of the oxide etch chamber. This is important because the lifetime extension has a significant impact on the cost of machine maintenance and machine uptime. This can potentially extend the lifetime of at least 30% more than the current lifetime.

articleTitle: Elimination of 3D NAND Through-Array Contact Shortage on Yield Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the development of a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) under array (CuA) structured 3D NAND memory, the through-array contact (TAC) process plays a critical and indispensable role in the operation of such devices. In this work, during the preliminary wafer acceptance test (WAT), a circuit short issue corresponding to TAC module along with significant yield loss is reported. Failure analysis reveals that abnormal leakage is caused by the insufficient isolation between the bottom of the TAC and the neighboring poly-silicon grounding layers. More detail analyses by physical profiles and the X-ray metrology technique indicate that it might be directly relate to the tilting behavior of patterning TAC in plasma etching. A promising solution to improve the plasma tilting behavior in etching is demonstrated and that managed to recover the product yield effectively.

articleTitle: Recurring Hotspot Detection in Lithography
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A recurring hotspots detection system has been implemented to highlight wafers with marginal hotspot below the Focus Spot Monitoring (FSM) threshold in the lithography process. The system plays a key role in early detection and reduces exposure to repeating hotspots that causes inline, sort, or electric test failure. Through image processing techniques and mathematical computations, the exposed wafers are highlighted in a monitoring chart and auto-disposition is triggered.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Assembly Test Automation and Standardization Research Association Plans, Goals and Simulation Results
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The SATAS (Semiconductor Assembly Test Automation and Standardization) Research Association was kicked off in April 2024. [1] SATAS is supported by the Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and includes 23 member companies, all with the joint goal of transforming conventional assembly test manufacturing by developing strategies to automate the manufacturing process. The consortia will initially develop standards to support the equipment, systems and interfaces necessary for automation. The new concepts will then be implemented in a pilot line to evaluate and demonstrate the standards and automation systems, as well as measure the labor savings and manufacturing efficiencies that automation enables. This paper describes the overall SATAS concepts, plans and goals, initial simulation results of the new automation concepts, as well as the goals and progress to date developing industry standards that will support the overall SATAS goals.

articleTitle: DUV-Vis-IR Optical Metrology Enhancements with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Machine learning algorithms can supplement traditional data analysis methods and enable new capabilities for optical metrology systems. This includes measurements of semiconductor processes that are difficult or not possible with the standard approach. By integrating standard models with machine learning, we leverage the strengths of both methodologies. This paper will provide three application examples, using UV-Vis-IR spectroscopic reflectance data, where machine learning adds significant value: 1) Lead (Pb) classification within a glass frit bonding layer, 2) Phosphorus content measurement within a TEOS film, and 3) CD measurements for a Deep Trench Isolation (DTI) structure.

articleTitle: Reduction of Energy Consumption through Fab Environment Control
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor Fabs consume substantial amounts of energy, mainly in the form of electric power, to operate manufacturing equipment and to rigorously control the environment in the Fab. For our Fab, which is located in a temperate climate, the demand on climate control changes with the seasons: in summer energy is used mainly to cool the cleanroom, but in winter the cleanroom needs to be kept warmer than the outside. Control of relative humidity (RH) is vital to maintaining the production process as well. Varying RH can lower energy consumption and cost, but can affect the production process in a number of ways. To avoid adverse effects we established a list of potential issues and a plan to prevent any deviations. We then varied RH in a controlled fashion and verified that production can continue without issues.

articleTitle: The incoming clean of raw silicon wafers: challenges, root causes and possible solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: An investigation of the cleaning efficiency of different raw wafer materials from different vendors is presented using a standard clean 1 and standard clean 2 incoming cleaning procedure. It will be discussed whether the observed material and vendor dependency is caused by the incoming clean, the used manufacturing tools or by the wafer material itself. By using particle and contact angle measurements, QCEPT, REM and EDX, significant variations of the raw wafer surface were found before and after the incoming clean. Thus, an analysis of the entire raw wafer supply chain was performed including production, packaging, transport and unpackaging of the wafers. A determination of the root cause of the observed cleaning inefficiencies was possible and solutions to overcome the apparent cleaning inefficiency could be derived.

articleTitle: Optimization Epitaxy Process to Reduce Hotspot Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Silicon epitaxy is critical for customizing film resistivity and enhancing breakdown voltage in advanced automotive devices. However, process-induced wafer non-uniformity can lead to downstream lithography defocus and hotspots. In this paper, we demonstrate two methods to mitigate the problem: inserting a silicon oxide capping layer to suppress parasitic growth at wafer edge; optimizing epitaxial temperature from 1080 °C to 1000 °C to improve film uniformity. The combined approach eliminates wafer edge roll-up profile, establishes a globally flat wafer surface and achieves a 95% reduction of lithography hotspots.

articleTitle: Predicting Seal Longevity: Advanced Simulations for Plasma and Rotary Applications in Semiconductor Processes : EO: Equipment Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In many semiconductor manufacturing processes, ensuring vacuum integrity is critical to achieving optimal tool performance. Elastomers, particularly perfluoroelastomers (FFKMs), are widely employed in both static and dynamic sealing applications within high-end semiconductor equipment due to their resilience in harsh operating conditions such as chemical plasma. However, designing and optimizing each component of semiconductor equipment can be time-intensive, particularly when determining effective preventive maintenance (PM) cycles. The present contribution describes a finite element method to predict seal lifetime in two separate systems where material loss is a primary failure mode; abrasive wear of a rotary seal in a vacuum pump, and a static FFKM seal in a plasma etching application.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Analysis Approach Through Strategic Application of t-Tests: A Case Study in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The explosive growth in data volumes due to a paradigm shift in manufacturing and engineering processes by the advent of industry 4.0 has made it impossible for an engineer to examine all investigation outcomes with manual labour alone. This technological revolution necessitates a concomitant evolution in our analytical methodologies to effectively address the increased complexity, volume, and velocity of data generation. In this work, using Sort Parametric analyses as a case study, we demonstrate the strategic application of statistical methods in product engineering, offering insights into the practical implementation of t-tests/ Anova as a powerful and effective tool for screening big data analyses to enhance efficiency in our data-driven decision-making cycles, aiding in process optimization and anomaly detections.

articleTitle: Process Challenges attributing to Lithography Overlay Misalignment : A Case Study on BEOL Lithography Process
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Photolithography is one of the most complex and critical processes in semiconductor wafer fabrication. It plays a key role in achieving high resolution, high photoresist sensitivity, minimal feature sizes, precise process control, and low defect density.[1] As technology continues to shrink, yield improvement has become a major challenge in wafer fabrication. In particular, edge die yield loss remains a critical issue in semiconductor manufacturing. Within the lithography process, this yield loss is often caused by pattern uniformity issues, pattern distortion, resist lifting, and defocus.[1] To monitor wafer performance and predict yield, methods such as Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Advanced Process Control (APC) are widely used. However, yield loss can still happen even when all inline monitor reports values within specification limits.This study examines a case study in the Back-End-of-Line (BEOL) lithography process, where significant yield loss occurred despite Overlay and critical dimension (CD) measurements being within specification limits. The primary cause was a misalignment between the via and metal-metal layers, exacerbated by slightly larger via CD and a sloped upstream metal profile at wafer edge. As a result, vias landed improperly on the metal, particularly in line-on-line structures on the wafer edge, leading to yield loss, causing circuit short or reliability concern.This study highlights the need for enhanced monitoring techniques and process control strategies to mitigate variations and improve overall yield in semiconductor manufacturing. This paper also proposes a new inline monitor method to combine the upstream and downstream factors and automatically trigger mask rework to predict yield loss.

articleTitle: Process Optimizations for GDDR SGRAM in Automotive Applications : Topic: DI: Defect Inspection and Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: An investigation into latent failures due to the formation of a resistive interface at the metal-to-via connection in automotive grade graphics SGRAM. Process improvements in via formation, increased electrical coverage targeting signal degradation, and wafer level analysis to prevent test escapes during production have been proposed. This paper aims to provide insight into the manufacturing process of graphics DRAM to target the formation of kinks near the metal-to-via connection during the wet etch clean step to prevent the formation of the resistive interface.

articleTitle: Enabling 3D Integration: Full pattern wafer die shape characterization using Wave Front Phase Imaging at 8μm lateral resolution
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a case study on the enhancement of 3D integration through Wave Front Phase Imaging (WFPI) shape measurements, enabling precise die shape characterization with 8μm lateral resolution. A full-pattern wafer analysis at the end of the line is demonstrated, providing high-accuracy measurements of individual dies. These measurements are essential for ensuring optimal alignment and compatibility in 3D integrated circuits (ICs), thereby improving stacking accuracy and overall performance. As 3D ICs become increasingly critical in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, the ability to achieve precise die shape characterization will play a pivotal role in future technological advancements.

articleTitle: Effect of plasma RF state 0 pulsing power on micro-loading and cross-wafer uniformity in high aspect ratio contact etch
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: High aspect ratio contact (HARC) etch is a critical process to build capacitors and contacts in DRAM memory. Slight change in wafer uniformity and micro-loading very often affects yield and device performance. In the paper we present the results of improving cross-wafer uniformity and micro-loading between different shapes and sizes of contacts by using a new radio frequency (RF) state 0 pulsing power. With proper setting of the state 0 pulsing power, anti-fuse under etch has been successfully eliminated.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Etching Architecture Refinement from Small Data in 3D NAND Development
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This study demonstrates a promising approach for optimizing as-etched structures using an artificial intelligence (AI) model built on a small dataset collected from specific plasma etching conditions. Through advanced optimization with AI-assisted tuning, the resulting vertical channel (VC) structure of 3D NAND effectively minimizes shape deformation and contributes to enhanced reliability performance in 3D NAND device operation.

articleTitle: Denuded Zone Formation by High Temperature Inert Anneal of 300 mm Cz-Silicon Wafers : AEPM: Advanced Equipment, Processes and Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We investigated the influence of high temperature inert anneals (1150° - 1175°C) in nitrogen and argon on the formation of an oxygen denuded zone (DZ) in 300 mm as-grown Czochralski Silicon (Cz-Si) wafers from three different vendors as an alternative to epitaxial layers as active device zone. An anneal process optimized in time, temperature and gas ambient was found, resulting in a significant reduction in STI etch defects caused by bulk micro defects (BMD). Changes in the Oxygen interstitial concentration were studied as well as the effect of the high temperature anneal on slip line formation. We discuss the underlying mechanisms of the BMD anneal and DZ formation.

articleTitle: CPEC Clean Enhancement via Backside Polishing to Reduce Precoat UPC Fault
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The lifetime of the clampable protective ESC cover (CPEC) of the Novellus SPEED<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> high-density plasma (HDP) chemical vapor deposition (CVD) tool has been investigated. It was found that backside average roughness (Ra) increases over time. This leads to helium leakage and causes universal pressure controller (UPC) faults. Although the cover is sent for recycling, its performance deteriorates as the recycling count increases. The backside R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> does not reduce significantly after cleaning. This results in high backside R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> in recycled covers. By polishing the backside of the cover, the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> is greatly reduced. This improves the cover's survivability and reduces the precoat UPC fault rate. On a smoother surface, helium is well trapped due to the good contact between the cover and the ESC edge seal during the precoat deposition process. Fault trend results were gathered for 6 consecutive months. It was observed that once cleaned covers polished to lower R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> were installed in the tools, the precoat UPC fault rate reduced by 71.4 %. Typically, polishing the backside of the cover is effective in improving its reusability. It reduces the backside R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> to a low baseline. This allows for higher usage and lower failure rates.

articleTitle: Copper Residue Removal from Electrostatic Chuck to Mitigate Helium Leak Faults Using Enhanced In-Situ Chamber Clean : EO: Equipment Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In traditional CMOS, Copper (Cu) and Aluminum (Al-0.5%Cu) are predominantly used for back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnects and Metal Cap, Cu is used widely for interconnect wiring due to its superior electrical properties and better scalability, however Aluminum (Al-0.5%Cu) is preferred choice for Metal cap layer commonly known as the bond pad due to its cost-effectiveness and better wire bonding compatibilities. The formation of Metal cap is carried out in plasma dry aluminum etch tools. These dry etch processing chambers are susceptible to higher helium leak faults due to Cu contamination, primarily Cu residues on the electrostatic chuck (ESC) induced by wafer backside. This paper investigates effective mitigation strategies for helium leak faults by employing in-situ chamber cleaning techniques to remove Cu residues from the ESC surface. The proposed method of in-situ chamber cleaning aims to maintain the cleanliness of the etch chamber and ESC, hence reducing helium leak incidents and maintaining process stability

articleTitle: Improving Machine Calibration Performance through Systematic Feature Design in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing, discrepancies between the golden and target machines can lead to inconsistencies in product quality and reduced yield, highlighting the need for more effective calibration methods. Traditionally, machine calibration relies on using basic statistical features during the feature extraction step, which limits the ability to fully capture the complex characteristics of machine dynamics. This study aims to expand the spectrum of feature types that contribute to enhancing machine calibration performance. Experiments using a Hitachi Plasma Etching System demonstrate that the new method significantly reduces overall calibration errors, representing more than a twofold improvement over the traditional approach. This enhanced calibration accuracy ensures greater consistency between machines and manufacturing processes, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and minimizing downtime.

articleTitle: Characterization of Electroless Palladium Precipitates Induced by Water-Ligand Interactions
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This study examines the effects of water-ligand molar ratios and agitation speeds on the formation of Pd precipitates in electroless plating processes, aiming to optimize conditions for high-quality metal coatings in ENEPIG applications. Different water-ligand molar ratios were investigated, revealing that higher ratios increase Pd precipitation and result in more pronounced precipitate shapes. The proposed mechanism indicates that the central Pd(II) ion, coordinated by ligands, forms a stable complex that reduces rapid precipitation. However, at elevated water-ligand molar ratios, ligand dissociation exposes coordination sites, leading to the formation of aqua complexes that are more susceptible to hydrolysis, which in turn accelerates the nucleation and growth of Pd precipitates. XRD analysis showed that the smaller crystallite size (28.67 nm) at a water-ligand molar ratio of < 5 indicates slower, more controlled Pd precipitation, while the larger size (43.01 nm) at a ratio of 150 suggests rapid nucleation and growth. Agitation speed significantly influences precipitate characteristics; while an optimal speed of 100 rpm results in powder and 250 rpm yields black solids, higher speeds of 800 rpm lead to less precipitation and shiny metal-colored precipitates. Overall, this research highlights the critical roles of water-ligand molar ratios and agitation speeds in controlling precipitate quality to prevent operational challenges, offering valuable insights for optimizing electroless plating techniques beyond Pd and enhancing metal coatings for semiconductor applications.

articleTitle: A Tool Grouping-Based Approach to Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Predictive Maintenance in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work examines the use of tool grouping strategies in Fleet Learning and Transfer Learning to enhance predictive maintenance strategies for semiconductor manufacturing tools, particularly in cases of data insufficiency. The challenge of domain dissimilarity between tools, which can lead to negative transfer and unreliable predictions, is addressed through the selection of similar tools for training. By employing various tool grouping strategies, the approach aims to reduce noise and improve the accuracy and stability of remaining useful life predictions. A comparative analysis evaluates the impact of these grouping techniques across different data conditions, highlighting that the effectiveness of tool grouping varies depending on the specific data characteristics and tool conditions. These findings suggest that the success of tool grouping is contingent on factors such as data availability, the uniqueness of tool features, and the degree of similarity between the target and source tools.

articleTitle: Sequence-Aware Inline Measurement Attribution for Good-Bad Wafer Diagnosis : DM: Big Data Management and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: How can we identify problematic upstream processes when a certain type of wafer defect starts appearing at a quality checkpoint? Given the complexity of modern semiconductor manufacturing, which involves thousands of process steps, cross-process root cause analysis for wafer defects has been considered highly challenging. This paper proposes a novel framework called Trajectory Shapley Attribution (TSA), an extension of Shapley values (SV), a widely used attribution algorithm in explainable artificial intelligence research. TSA overcomes key limitations of standard SV, including its disregard for the sequential nature of manufacturing processes and its reliance on an arbitrarily chosen reference point. We applied TSA to a good-bad wafer diagnosis task in experimental front-end-of-line processes at the NY CREATES Albany NanoTech fab, aiming to identify measurement items (serving as proxies for process parameters) most relevant to abnormal defect occurrence.

articleTitle: Modeling resources in research and development semiconductor manufacturing shop floors
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Research and Development (R&D) semiconductor manufacturing systems differ from production facilities in various aspects, including the level of characterization and control over engineering processes, the scales of production control, and the range of automatable decision-making processes. As part of an ultimate goal to expand process capabilities and activity volume, this paper focuses on the explicit modeling of resources and their associated states in an R&D shop floor. Three types of resources are characterized and modeled, and their capabilities are analyzed: knowledge about engineering processes (resp., device team holds), workforce (resp., the number of equivalent operators), and machinery (resp., time to repair, time between failures). Particular attention is paid to the variability and granularity, under and out of control, of key aspects characterizing the resources of interest and their impact on operations management decisions. Numerical experiments are conducted and analyzed based on real-life instances.

articleTitle: In-line Raman spectroscopy for semiconductors strain engineering and control : Topic/Category AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Raman spectroscopy has been used for decades in academic and industrial laboratories. This rapid, non-invasive and non-destructive technique provides valuable information on material properties such as composition, crystallinity, strain/stress, doping, crystallographic orientation and structural type. Recent advancements in instrumentation have demonstrated the potential of Raman spectroscopy to meet the demands of the semiconductor industry, leading to a significant increase interest in using it as an in-line metrology solution. In this work, we present specific use cases of Raman spectroscopy for in-line metrology in the semiconductor field. More precisely, we evaluate strain/stress and crystalline quality of ultrathin Si and Ge films at the wafer scale. This study highlights the relevance of Raman spectroscopy as an in-line metrology solution in cleanroom environments for semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Simulation-based Evaluation of Idle Vehicle Positioning on Logistics Performance in OHT Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper investigates the idle vehicle positioning problem in Overhead Hoist Transport (OHT) systems, commonly used in the semiconductor manufacturing industry. We present a mathematical model for dynamically reallocating idle vehicles to optimal locations, aiming to reduce expected retrieve distances and improve overall logistics efficiency. Given the computational challenges of solving the model exactly, we propose heuristic approaches based on the k-median problem. These approaches are evaluated through simulation experiments, which demonstrate that median-based idle vehicle positioning can significantly enhance logistics performance. However, frequent reallocations can lead to congestion and reduce system efficiency, particularly in high-demand scenarios.

articleTitle: Event-Based Sampling Architecture and Optimization for Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The proposed paper will present a standardized solution for Industrial IoT, to employ event-based sampling for detecting equipment faults and preventing product impact in large-scale manufacturing. This is important because IoT sensors can generate dense datasets with wide distributions, attributed to varying operating conditions in the fab; sensor measurements summarized without the appropriate context makes it difficult to correlate IoT data with fab processes. To improve our detection rate and minimize false alarms, it is critical to intelligently sample this data using contextual events before applying tighter control. We implemented a standardized solution for event-based sampling which is easily extensible to any Industrial IoT scenario, since it was designed and optimized using industry best practices and evaluated against real fab use-cases. It significantly reduced server CPU consumption and prevented message loss / connection timeouts with other manufacturing systems. Improving our signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) based on context consequentially helped with tighter process-control, enhanced fab operations, and transformed our detection from reactive to predictive / preventive.

articleTitle: Developing an Ambidextrous Workforce for Profitable Nanoscale Manufacturing: The Case of Semiconductor Joint Development Projects
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: An exploratory, qualitative, empirical study of joint development projects (JDPs) in semiconductor manufacturing suggests that chipmakers and tool suppliers are facing major ambidexterity challenges, i.e., they are having problems balancing the need to exploit with the need to explore. The relentless escalation of the economies of speed, scale, and scope that drive the semiconductor industry has reached the point where individuals, teams, and organizations can no longer create, transfer, and absorb knowledge at a rate that guarantees profitability. The investigation of ambidexterity that is described in this paper provides a novel, knowledge-oriented approach to workforce development. This approach leads to a set of best practices, which are being and should be deployed by chipmakers and their suppliers so that these firms remain profitable in the production of chips that exhibit nanoscale features.

articleTitle: Toward ML-enhanced Design and Fabrication of Resonant Nanoelectromechanical IR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This study introduces a novel approach for optimizing the design of ScAIN-based tethered nanoplate resonators with enhanced sensitivity, bandwidth, and thermal efficiency for infrared sensing applications. Without active cooling, achieving uncompromised IR sensor requirements necessitates an advanced design strategy to optimize the design parameter space. We used a feature-based ML approach to learn the design parameters of the nanoplate resonator. A data set encompassing layout (geometric) parameters (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>, S, C), measured resonator parameters (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, Q, $k_t^2$), and Butterworth-Van Dyke (BVD) fitting results (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf>) was collected from 288 ScAIN-based IR sensing tethered nanoplate resonators using the automated RF measurement setup, at various RF power levels (-5, -10, -15 and -20 dBm). We demonstrated that the Random Forest model yields the best results among the other machine learning algorithms tested, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.59 MHz and a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 3.36, with an R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) value of 0.98, indicating an excellent model fit. Using the trained Random Forest method, we demonstrated design exploration (interpolation) for target resonator quality factors. These results underscore the efficacy of the ML-guided design optimization approach in advancing next-generation thermal detector performance for IR sensing applications.

articleTitle: Neurosymbolic AI-Driven Zero-Defect Manufacturing in Semiconductor Assembly: A Hybrid Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative framework for defect diagnosis and quality control in semiconductor manufacturing using neurosymbolic AI. By integrating knowledge graphs, ontologies, and deep neural networks, the approach harmonizes human expertise and machine learning to predict, diagnose, and mitigate defects in real time. Focusing on Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and other expert sources, the research transforms this knowledge into structured physics-aware ontologies and knowledge graphs to enable seamless integration with neural networks. Additionally, novel ensemble neural network architectures are explored to leverage the full potential of physics-aware neurosymbolic techniques. The proposed framework enhances defect prediction and root cause analysis and also paves the way for more interpretable and adaptive AI-driven quality control systems in semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: Curricula, Courses, Labs and Software for Maximum Semiconductor Manufacturing Experience
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper will describe how Rochester Institute of Technology provides semiconductor manufacturing experiences in a university setting, utilizing lectures, cleanroom tools, cooperative work experience, and collaborative use of appropriate software. For over 40 years these efforts have served as a model for other programs but not enough new programs have been created to close the continuing workforce gaps. It is important to increase the supply of innovative engineers entering the field with "lab to fab" experience. These engineers need to hit the ground running instead of requiring years to acquire the necessary experience. Two software platforms discussed in this paper can be easily used by resource limited programs in conjunction with RIT generated data and expertise to provide key experience levels for students before entering industry.

articleTitle: Wafer Defect Root Cause Analysis with Partial Trajectory Regression DM: Big Data Management and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Identifying upstream processes responsible for wafer defects is challenging due to the combinatorial nature of process flows and the inherent variability in processing routes, which arises from factors such as rework operations and random process waiting times. This paper presents a novel framework for wafer defect root cause analysis, called Partial Trajectory Regression (PTR). The proposed framework is carefully designed to address the limitations of conventional vector-based regression models, particularly in handling variable-length processing routes that span a large number of heterogeneous physical processes. To compute the attribution score of each process given a detected high defect density on a specific wafer, we propose a new algorithm that compares two counterfactual outcomes derived from partial process trajectories. This is enabled by new representation learning methods, proc2vec and route2vec. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework using real wafer history data from the NY CREATES fab in Albany.

articleTitle: An Inherently Explainable Approach for Reinforcement Learning Based Dispatching in Semiconductor Frontend Fabs
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Scheduling is a crucial task in many manufacturing environments. Depending on the type of the manufactured product, a multitude of different properties and constraints complicate the already complex structure of a job-shop scheduling problem. Semiconductor Manufacturing is well known to be one of the most complex production processes, namely for its stochastic nature, diverse product mix, which leads to strict tool dedications, and for the presence of re-entrant flows in the production line. In this paper, we propose an approach for finding a dispatching policy through the use of (NN), whose weights are optimized through an Evolution Strategies method called (CMA-ES), able to minimize the tardiness, throughput and other relevant metrics within a digital twin of a real-world, stochastic, large-scale semiconductor manufacturing facility.

articleTitle: GPU-Accelerated Feature Extraction for Real-Time Vision AI and LLM Systems Efficiency: Autonomous Image Segmentation, Unsupervised Clustering, and Smart Pattern Recognition for Scalable AI Processing with 6.6× Faster Performance, 2.5× Higher Accuracy, and UX-Centric UI Boosting Human-in-the-Loop Productivity
publicationTitle: 2025 36th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The high computational cost of digital image processing, requiring high-performance hardware and extensive resources, severely limits real-time applications. While advancements in algorithm design and GPU acceleration have significantly improved efficiency, modern AI-driven applications such as large language models (LLMs), Generative AI (GenAI), medical imaging, autonomous vehicle perception, photography, advanced nano-scale semiconductor metrology, satellite image analysis, high-precision manufacturing, robotics, and real-time anomaly detection, still demand further optimization to reduce computational overhead and improve scalability.In this paper, we introduce GPU-Accelerated Feature Extraction to enhance runtime and efficiency in edge-based simulations. Our approach leverages AI-driven clustering, grouping images with similar visual and pattern characteristics to enable adaptive tuning on a small subset before generalizing across the full dataset. This method achieves a 3.78× reduction in runtime.Furthermore, rather than processing an entire image, we recognize and extract a single representative pattern or region of interest (ROI) per image, removing redundant data and background noise. This refinement results in an additional 1.74× runtime improvement, culminating in an overall 6.6× speed boost, enhancing Scalable Real-Time AI Processing. We also demonstrated that with a similar runtime, the accuracy achieved is 2.5× higher.This solution, integrated into Calibre SEMSuite™, supports multicloud and real-time deployment for enhanced scalability, usability, and performance, providing users with a powerful tool for fully automated, AI-driven image classification, making high-throughput image review feasible even at the scale required for cutting-edge applications.Beyond performance gains, this approach introduces autonomous data cleaning, anomaly detection and defect identification mechanism, allowing failed patterns and defective images to be identified without human intervention, boosting the reviewer productivity.As GenAI and LLM systems gain popularity, the computational demands on modern systems have reached unprecedented levels. As we demonstrate, thanks to feature extraction and ROI selection, instead of needing for the entire dataset to be processed, only a fraction of the data could be used. This is crucial for reducing the computational overhead of LLM systems.We demonstrate that our method enables high-precision, real-time AI inference with applications in computer vision, LLMs, autonomous systems, healthcare, and scalable AI computing.
